# Fixed C exec and descendant CPU observations

Two separate, once-only N1-1 CPU cases returned narrow success for a fixed G guardian → X/E worker → D descendant tree. X and E are the same process before and after exec into a second product. Source A `5574bc65604dda7ba34b2f54b261fa07353da02e` was pushed and integrated through [PR46](https://github.com/Zefan-Cai/Open-Jev/pull/46), merge `88f2e205a314b3b96a1918534f9499e805c66d2e`, before either MS case. [Source documentation](https://github.com/Zefan-Cai/Open-Jev/blob/5574bc65604dda7ba34b2f54b261fa07353da02e/docs/frontier-v8-owned-c-exec-descendant.md) defines the closed protocol. Outer Python, compiler and linker activity is additional.

| Case | Returned parent-owned wait and adoption | Directed signals |
| --- | --- | --- |
| normal | E729543 reaped D729544/raw0; G729542 reaped E/raw0. G_D wait was uncalled. | 0 |
| worker_loss | G732322 reaped E732323/raw9, independently observed the same D732324 change parent E→G, then reaped adopted D/raw9. E_D wait was uncalled. | G_E and G_D each one original-handle pidfd SIGKILL attempt, flags0/result0/errno0 |

Each case built fresh, distinct guardian and leaf products, reported as 84,736 and 44,944 bytes. The joint exec gate combined private error-pipe EOF, postexec READY, startup FD facts and independent same-PID/birth/boot/UID/PPID product transition. `EXEC_ENTER` alone is prospective. Returned `exec_protocol` reports attempted=true, returned=false, with result/errno null; it does not invent a successful returning fexecve call. Two preexec PRODUCT_CHECK packets were bound before PRE_READY; their unreturned fstat payload tuples were not separately decoded. G_E was acquired before exec and never reopened. D creation and binding followed the completed product transition.

G observed its own subreaper GET0→SET1→GET1; X/E and D separately reported GET0. Startup exec-error EOF, required READY/ARM/ACK gates and live identity checks preceded primary FINISH/signal. Terminal parent-report EOF and loss EOF followed the corresponding actions. Normal E alone waited for D. Loss G first signaled and reaped E, then separately observed D's adoption before signaling and waiting for D. Signal budgets were consumed immediately before each syscall, with no retry and no negative cleanup signals. Three original pidfds are G_E, G_D and E_D. The two guardian pidfds had explicit once-close and immediate F_GETFD=-1/EBADF; normal E_D also did. Loss E_D has only killed-owner teardown, without an observed explicit close/EBADF.

Each case has 40 FD provenance rows and 25 FD flag rows. Normal: 29 explicit once-close, 6 original absent, 3 exec-entry closed and 2 parent-report EOF. Loss: 24 explicit once-close, 6 original absent, 3 exec-entry closed, 5 owner death and 2 unreturned loss close. These categories are separate evidence; owner death and unreturned close are not invented syscall returns. New child pipe numbers 0/1/2 are legal by their semantic generation and do not reopen original handles or budgets. The cases returned 71/59 packets. G reset its own subreaper SET0→GET0 only after exact terminal/reap/FD/time predicates. Shared work/cleanup/terminal/Gtotal/child-expiry offsets are 5/8/10/12/14 seconds; self-expiry is not an observed recovery result.
